claims.text: Dynamic formation and regeneration of a protective multicomponent oxide film governs the coupled tribo-corrosion response.
A protective chromium oxide layer and high-entropy spinel can form after thermal treatment at 800 °C.
Constituent elements in the coating can act as sacrificial anodes and protect the SS-304 substrate.
The initial material is an equiatomic Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 high-entropy-alloy cladding on SS-304.
The as-produced Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 cladding has a homogeneous microstructure.
The alloy contains elements capable of rapid oxide formation under thermal or wear activation.
Elevated temperature or thermal cycling will promote protective surface-oxide formation during sliding in a corrosive medium.
A mixed scale containing Cr2O3 and spinel oxides develops on worn surfaces.
Wear-induced exposure periodically refreshes the mixed oxide scale.
Sliding mechanically removes surface material and exposes fresh alloy regions.
Freshly exposed chromium rapidly oxidizes into a thin, continuous film that slows localized corrosion.
The regenerated oxide film limits ingress of corrosive species.
The oxide film reduces wear by increasing local surface hardness.
A pre-established or rapidly regenerating oxide film will reduce combined wear-corrosion mass loss relative to a matched non-oxidized baseline.
A pre-established or rapidly regenerating oxide film will reduce corrosion-pit density.
The oxide-protected sample's wear will become dominated by mild adhesive removal rather than severe abrasive or oxidative degradation.
The protective mechanism holds when oxide regeneration keeps pace with removal and the environment stabilizes the oxide.
The mechanism fails at extreme loads, excessive wear rates, or under chemistry that continuously disrupts oxide formation.
Failure of oxide-bearing samples to show significantly lower wear and corrosion metrics, or failure to observe a persistent continuous oxide, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The specified equiatomic Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Cu cladding contains no Cr, yet Cr is described as a reactive element in the alloy and Cr2O3 formation is central to the proposed mechanism. Any chromium would have to originate from the SS-304 substrate or from an unstated composition.
